findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and get canceled when the request returns
findings.body: Each background goroutine builds its context with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` from the incoming request context. The method returns as soon as the unified-storage write succeeds, and the apiserver then cancels the request context. That cancellation reaches the derived context, so the legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection is often aborted or never runs (same pattern at lines 110, 135, 163). Legacy storage silently drifts from unified storage, which defeats the stated 'safe measure'. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Legacy write failures in background goroutines are never logged
findings.body: The goroutines only record a duration metric with an error flag. The error itself is discarded in Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection. The old code logged legacy failures. Now a divergence between legacy and unified storage leaves no trace of which object failed or why.

findings.title: Storage create failure recorded as a legacy duration
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`. Unified-storage failures are therefore reported as legacy failures. The same mistake is in Update at line 129.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as a storage duration
findings.body: The background legacy DeleteCollection calls `d.recordStorageDuration` rather than `recordLegacyDuration`. Each delete-collection is counted twice as a storage operation and never as a legacy one, which skews both metric series.

findings.title: Object name used as the metric 'kind' label in Delete
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object name where the kind belongs. Every object name becomes a separate label value, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality and wrong kind attribution. It should be `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Delete puts the base logger in context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` stores the base logger rather than `log`. Downstream storage logs therefore lack the name, kind and method values, unlike the other methods.

findings.title: Legacy update re-applies objInfo against legacy state instead of the unified result
findings.body: The previous code wrapped the unified-storage result in `updateWrapper`, so legacy received exactly the object written to unified storage. Now the raw `objInfo` is replayed in a goroutine, and the update or patch is applied to whatever old object legacy holds. For PATCH/apply, or when the stores already differ, legacy ends up with different content than unified storage. Reusing `objInfo` concurrently after the request has finished is also unsafe.

findings.title: Request object shared with a background goroutine while the handler keeps using it
findings.body: `obj` and `options` are passed to `d.Legacy.Create` in a goroutine after the method has already returned `created`, which may be the same pointer or derived from `obj`. The apiserver goes on encoding or mutating the response while legacy storage reads or mutates the same object, which is a data race. The object should be deep-copied before handing it to the goroutine.

findings.title: Unit tests never verify the async legacy write and race with it
findings.body: The tests return right after the dual-writer call without waiting for the background goroutine, so nothing asserts that the legacy write happens. Legacy and storage mocks share a single `mock.Mock`, so expectations meant for one store satisfy calls to the other. For example, the 'unified store fails' Create case only fails because the legacy expectation for `failingObj` is matched by the storage call. A goroutine can also invoke the mock after the subtest finishes.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests check legacy reads immediately after async writes
findings.body: `doPlaylistTests` creates or updates through k8s and then immediately queries the legacy `/api/playlists` endpoints via `getFromBothAPIs` and the search check. In mode 3 the legacy write is asynchronous, so these assertions race the background goroutine. If the legacy endpoint reads legacy storage, the test will be flaky; if it reads unified storage, legacy consistency is not being tested at all.
